sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ernmas was an Irish mother goddess and an obscure one. She is most known for her children. She bore the three land goddesses, Fólla, Banba, and Ériu. Some ancient texts give her as Éirinn instead. She also appears as the mother of the triple war goddesses. These were Machao, Badb, and the Mórrígan. Koch notes that Bodb, Macha, and the Morrígan sit among her daughters. Her name connects to the modern Irish word of use. The word embas means death by iron or death by weapons.
